title: Trigonometry in three dimensions
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:20Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point is about finding right-angled triangles inside 3D shapes, while the closest bank point covers two flat 2D triangles that share a side, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Trigonometry in three dimensions
card: A 3D shape holds right-angled triangles. Pick one, then redraw it flat and label its sides. Work in one flat triangle at a time.
For a box 3 by 4 by 12, the diagonal across the base is a hypotenuse. It is \(\sqrt{3^{2} + 4^{2}} = 5\).
That base diagonal is now a side of a second right-angled triangle, with the height 12 as the other side. The diagonal through the box is \(\sqrt{5^{2} + 12^{2}} = 13\).
To find the angle between that diagonal and the base, use the second triangle. \(\tan \theta = \frac{12}{5}\), so \(\theta \approx 67.4^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: Find a right-angled triangle, work out one side at a time, and reuse each answer in the next triangle.

a.q: A box is 6 cm long, 8 cm wide and 24 cm high. What is the length of the diagonal across its base?
a.why: The base is a right-angled triangle with sides 6 and 8, so the diagonal is \(\sqrt{6^{2} + 8^{2}} = 10\). A student who gets 26 cm has found the diagonal through the box, which needs the height too.
a.clue: The base is flat, so the height is not used.

b.q: A cable runs from one floor corner of a room to the opposite ceiling corner. The room is 12 m long, 9 m wide and 8 m high. What angle does the cable make with the floor?
b.why: The base diagonal is \(\sqrt{12^{2} + 9^{2}} = 15\). In the triangle with sides 15 and 8, \(\tan \theta = \frac{8}{15}\), so \(\theta \approx 28.1^{\circ}\). Using \(\frac{15}{8}\) gives 61.9°, the angle at the ceiling corner, not the floor.
b.clue: The angle sits next to the base diagonal, not a room edge.

wants.brief: A box with length 4, width 3 and height 12. Show the base diagonal of length 5 and the diagonal through the box of length 13, with the two right-angled triangles shaded and the angle θ between the long diagonal and the base marked.
wants.why: It shows where the two right-angled triangles sit inside the box.

check.summary: No problems found. All the values check out: the base diagonal of 10 cm, the cable's base diagonal of 15 m and its angle of about 28.1° with the floor, and the card's 5, 13 and 67.4°.
